title: Cell Parts Work as One Team

scenes.visual: Heart muscle cell crowded with orange mitochondria beside a white fat cell whose single drop swells; the essential question appears.
scenes.tts: At rest, your heart beats about sixty to one hundred times a minute. Its muscle cells are crowded with tiny parts called mitochondria. A white fat cell under your skin is different. It is mostly one big drop of stored fat. So what are the parts inside a cell? And how do they work together to keep it alive?

scenes.visual: A cell outline; grey small parts appear and are named organelles; nucleus turns blue and is labelled; membrane lights up with arrows in and out.
scenes.tts: Many cells contain organelles. An organelle is a small part inside a cell that does a special job. The nucleus holds the cell's main instructions. The cell membrane is the thin boundary around the cell. It controls what enters and leaves.

scenes.visual: Cytoplasm fills in and is labelled; endoplasmic reticulum folds in and passes proteins and fats; a vacuole takes in water, food and wastes.
scenes.tts: The cytoplasm is everything inside the cell membrane except the nucleus: a jelly-like fluid and the organelles in it. The endoplasmic reticulum is a network of folded membranes. It helps make and move many proteins and fats. A vacuole is a sac that stores water, food and wastes. It is large in plant cells. Many animal cells have only small sacs instead.

scenes.visual: A sugar (glucose) chip goes into a mitochondrion and energy leaves while the sugar chip stays; then metabolism with two example chips.
scenes.tts: Mitochondria release much of the energy stored in food. One kind of food is the sugar called glucose. Mitochondria release that energy in a form the cell can use. Metabolism means all the chemical reactions in the cell. Photosynthesis and cellular respiration are two examples.

scenes.visual: Nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria in one dashed system; instructions flow, proteins and fats come out, energy arrow from mitochondria; then the mitochondria stop and the output slows.
scenes.tts: The parts work together as one system. Instructions from the nucleus guide which proteins and fats are made. The endoplasmic reticulum makes and moves many of them. Mitochondria release the energy for this building. That building supports growth and repair. So trouble in one part slows many life processes.

scenes.visual: Heart and fat cells again with a column of five shared parts; amounts compared; closing line.
scenes.tts: Look again at the two cells. Both have a nucleus, a cell membrane, cytoplasm, endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria. The amounts are very different. A heart muscle cell works without a break. Mitochondria fill a large share of it. A white fat cell stores fat. One fat drop fills most of it. The other parts sit in a thin rim. So cells with different jobs hold different amounts of each part. Together, the parts keep the cell alive.
